subproblem.title: The bad set of centres has small Lebesgue measure (printed (1)–(4) of 5.1, 5-times covering)
subproblem.statement: Let ι be a finite index set with k := |ι| elements, E := ℝ^ι = EuclideanSpace ℝ ι with its Euclidean distance and Lebesgue measure L^k, (X, 𝒜) a measurable space, μ a finite measure on X, p : X → E measurable, g₀ ∈ E and β > 0. For g ∈ E and σ ∈ ℝ let T(g, σ) := {x ∈ X : there is z ∈ ℤ^ι with Σ_{i∈ι}(p(x)_i − g_i − z_i)² < σ²} (for σ > 0 this equals p⁻¹(⋃_{z∈ℤ^ι} B_σ(g + z))). Let Bad be the set of g ∈ E with |g − g₀| < 1/4 for which some σ with 0 < σ < 1/4 satisfies βσ^k·μ(X) < μ(T(g, σ)) (in [0, ∞]). Then L^k(Bad) ≤ 10^k/β, where L^k(Bad) is the outer Lebesgue measure (Bad is not assumed measurable).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X), IsFiniteMeasure μ → ∀ p : X → EuclideanSpace ℝ ι, Measurable p → ∀ (g₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) (β : ℝ), 0 < β → volume {g : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι | dist g g₀ < 1 / 4 ∧ ∃ σ : ℝ, 0 < σ ∧ σ < 1 / 4 ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (β * σ ^ Fintype.card ι) * μ univ < μ {x | ∃ z : ι → ℤ, ∑ i, (p x i - g i - z i) ^ 2 < σ ^ 2}} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (10 ^ Fintype.card ι / β)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, §5, printed "Proof of the Deformation Theorem", displays (1)–(4) and the estimate L^{n+1}(B_j) ≤ β⁻¹5^{n+1}ω_{n+1} that follows them (pp. 163–164), as reproduced in Steps 2–3 of the parent proof, with M(T ⌞ p_j⁻¹(·)) replaced by μ(p⁻¹(·)) for an arbitrary finite measure μ on X and measurable p : X → E (in the parent: X = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, μ = μ₁ or μ₂, E ≅ S_J via p = p_J, k = n + 1 = m + 2, g₀ = x_J = p_J(q)). Bad is the printed bad set B_j = (F_j ∩ B_{1/4}(x_j)) ∖ G_j with B_{1/4}(x_j) taken about g₀. Errata and details: the 5-times covering lemma (Simon Ch. 1, 3.4) is applied to closed balls; disjointness of the periodic tubes is proved as in Step 3 of the parent; the printed ω_k(5σ)^k is bounded by (10σ)^k (ω_k ≤ 2^k; the printed constants are not needed); measurability of Bad (Step 2 of the parent) is not needed, since the estimate is for the outer Lebesgue measure, which is countably subadditive on arbitrary sets.

Notation. For g ∈ E and z ∈ ℤ^ι write g + z for the point (g_i + z_i)_{i∈ι} of E; B_r(c) and B̄_r(c) are the open and closed Euclidean balls of E. Since |w − (g + z)|² = Σ_i (w_i − g_i − z_i)², T(g, σ) = p⁻¹(⋃_{z∈ℤ^ι} B_σ(g + z)) for every σ > 0 (only such σ occur below).

1. The tubes are measurable. For fixed g, σ and z the function w ↦ Σ_i (w_i − g_i − z_i)² is continuous on E, so {w ∈ E : Σ_i (w_i − g_i − z_i)² < σ²} is open. The union U(g, σ) over z ∈ ℤ^ι of these sets is open, hence Borel, and T(g, σ) = p⁻¹(U(g, σ)) is measurable because p is measurable.
2. The case μ(X) = 0. Then μ(T(g, σ)) ≤ μ(X) = 0 = βσ^k μ(X) for all g and σ, so the strict inequality in the definition of Bad never holds. Thus Bad = ∅ and L^k(Bad) = 0 ≤ 10^k/β. From now on assume μ(X) > 0; moreover μ(X) < ∞ because μ is finite.
3. Choice of radii (printed (3)). For each b ∈ Bad fix σ_b with 0 < σ_b < 1/4 and βσ_b^k μ(X) < μ(T(b, σ_b)).
4. Covering (printed (4)). The closed balls B̄_{σ_b}(b), b ∈ Bad, have radii at most 1/4. By the 5-times covering lemma (Simon Ch. 1, 3.4; the Vitali covering lemma, valid in every metric space for a family of closed balls with bounded radii) there is u ⊆ Bad such that the balls B̄_{σ_b}(b), b ∈ u, are pairwise disjoint and every B̄_{σ_g}(g), g ∈ Bad, is contained in B̄_{5σ_b}(b) for some b ∈ u. As g ∈ B̄_{σ_g}(g), we get Bad ⊆ ⋃_{b∈u} B̄_{5σ_b}(b).
5. The tubes of the subfamily are pairwise disjoint (printed: "p_j⁻¹ B_{σ_ℓ}(b_ℓ + z), ℓ = 1, 2, …, z ∈ ℤ^{n+ℓ} ∩ S_j, is a pairwise disjoint collection"). Let b ≠ b′ be in u and suppose x ∈ T(b, σ_b) ∩ T(b′, σ_{b′}). With y := p(x) there are z, z′ ∈ ℤ^ι with |y − (b + z)| < σ_b and |y − (b′ + z′)| < σ_{b′}.
   (a) If z = z′, the point w := y − z (coordinates y_i − z_i) satisfies |w − b| = |y − (b + z)| < σ_b and |w − b′| = |y − (b′ + z)| < σ_{b′}, so w ∈ B̄_{σ_b}(b) ∩ B̄_{σ_{b′}}(b′), contradicting the disjointness in step 4.
   (b) If z ≠ z′: as b, b′ ∈ Bad, |b − g₀| < 1/4 and |b′ − g₀| < 1/4, and σ_b, σ_{b′} < 1/4. Hence |y − (g₀ + z)| ≤ |y − (b + z)| + |b − g₀| < 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2 and similarly |y − (g₀ + z′)| < 1/2, i.e. B_{σ_b}(b + z) ⊆ B_{1/2}(g₀ + z) and B_{σ_{b′}}(b′ + z′) ⊆ B_{1/2}(g₀ + z′). Therefore |z − z′| = |(g₀ + z) − (g₀ + z′)| ≤ |(g₀ + z) − y| + |y − (g₀ + z′)| < 1. But z_i ≠ z′_i for some i, and then |z − z′| ≥ |z_i − z′_i| ≥ 1 because z_i − z′_i is a nonzero integer. Contradiction.
6. u is countable. The sets T(b, σ_b), b ∈ u, are measurable (step 1), pairwise disjoint (step 5) and of positive measure, because μ(T(b, σ_b)) > βσ_b^k μ(X) ≥ 0 (step 3). For each integer j ≥ 1, any finitely many of them with measure > 1/j have total measure ≤ μ(X) < ∞, so there are at most j·μ(X) of them; hence only countably many members of the family have positive measure. Since all of them do, u is countable.
7. Summation of (3) (printed: β Σ_ℓ σ_ℓ^{n+1} M(T) ≤ M(T)). By step 3, countable additivity of μ (u is countable, the T(b, σ_b) are measurable and pairwise disjoint) and monotonicity,
   Σ_{b∈u} βσ_b^k μ(X) ≤ Σ_{b∈u} μ(T(b, σ_b)) = μ(⋃_{b∈u} T(b, σ_b)) ≤ μ(X).
   Dividing by μ(X) ∈ (0, ∞) gives Σ_{b∈u} σ_b^k ≤ β⁻¹.
8. Volume of a ball. For c ∈ E and r ≥ 0, every w ∈ B̄_r(c) satisfies |w_i − c_i| ≤ |w − c| ≤ r for each i, so B̄_r(c) ⊆ ∏_{i∈ι} [c_i − r, c_i + r]. Lebesgue measure on E is the product Lebesgue measure in the coordinates, hence L^k(B̄_r(c)) ≤ (2r)^k (printed: ω_k r^k, and ω_k ≤ 2^k).
9. Conclusion (printed L^{n+1}(B_j) ≤ β⁻¹5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}). By step 4, countable subadditivity of the outer Lebesgue measure over the countable set u (step 6), step 8 with r = 5σ_b, and step 7:
   L^k(Bad) ≤ Σ_{b∈u} L^k(B̄_{5σ_b}(b)) ≤ Σ_{b∈u} (10σ_b)^k = 10^k Σ_{b∈u} σ_b^k ≤ 10^k/β. ∎
proof_key_steps: T(g, σ) is measurable (for σ > 0 it equals p⁻¹(⋃_z B_σ(g + z))); if μ(X) = 0 then Bad = ∅.
For b ∈ Bad choose σ_b ∈ (0, 1/4) with βσ_b^k μ(X) < μ(T(b, σ_b)) (printed (3)).
5-times covering: a disjoint subfamily {B̄_{σ_b}(b)}_{b∈u} with Bad ⊆ ⋃_{b∈u} B̄_{5σ_b}(b) (printed (4)).
The tubes T(b, σ_b), b ∈ u, are pairwise disjoint: equal z contradicts the ball disjointness; distinct z is impossible as B_{σ_b}(b + z) ⊆ B_{1/2}(g₀ + z).
u is countable (disjoint sets of positive measure in a finite measure space), and summing (3) gives Σ_{b∈u} σ_b^k ≤ 1/β.

audit.reason: The contract includes every required hypothesis and matches the prose. All nine proof steps are sound: measurable tubes, the zero-mass case, bounded-radius five-times covering, lattice-based disjointness, countability, cancellation of positive finite total mass, and the cube-volume estimate yield exactly 10^card(ι)/β. No measurability of Bad or positive-dimensional assumption is needed. The proof is complete and non-circular.
